report:
Reviewed the complete query_value claim, its one ordinary implementation association in sage-stash/src/lib.rs, and its complete one-test set. Requirements are (1) a stash-owned tree constitutes one incremental value, (2) Salsa compares and backdates the Stashed root as a unit, (3) children do not gain independent tracked identities, and (4) finer boundaries belong to external semantic queries rather than internal handles. No TODO or N/A evidence exists or is needed for these aspects.

Implementation: Stashed owns the stash, root and cached fingerprint together. Stashed::new hashes reachable root content through FingerprintHasher; pointer and slice traversal hashes child contents (including slice length and ordering) rather than allocation indices. Stashed equality compares this single fingerprint. Its feature-gated salsa::Update retains the entire old value and returns false on equality, or replaces the entire stash/root/fingerprint and returns true on change. Ptr and Slice hold ordinary stash-local indices, not Salsa tracked entities; indexing requires the owning stash and does not create database dependencies. Their Update implementations only compare local indices and do not introduce tracked identities. The source explicitly restricts reflection indices to within-stash use, not semantic cross-revision identities. The whole implementation file was inspected, including the helpers underlying hashing, storage, and indexing; no additional production source association is necessary for this claim.

Test adequacy: captured the entire incremental.rs file with review read to inspect Database, Input, produce, consume and execution recording helpers. The producer returns a whole Stashed<Slice<Ptr<u32>>> while the consumer is a separate tracked semantic query returning a scalar. Internal nodes remain ordinary stash allocations. The annotated test visibly checks initial value 21 and executions consume/produce, warm reuse with no executions, an allocation-layout change with producer-only execution and unchanged value, reachable content change yielding 41 and producer/consumer execution, and an unread-input change with no executions. The layout variant introduces an unreachable allocation and reverses child allocation order, so its backdating assertion would catch incorrectly comparing handles or arena layout. The reachable-value assertion would catch incorrectly suppressing all updates. This demonstrates the root boundary and an external semantic query boundary without making internal handles tracked identities; the structural absence of tracked node types was also checked directly in the implementation. All meaningful assertions are visible in the annotated body.

Executed cargo test -p sage-stash --features salsa --test incremental: one test passed, zero failed. The test file is gated by the salsa feature, explicitly enabled in that command. Source review and this focused runtime check establish the assessment; no workspace-wide run is claimed. Captured review policy via review read. No source files were modified and no requested edits remain.
